title: Storm-0501
summary: Storm-0501 is a Microsoft-assigned designation for a financially motivated intrusion set that public reporting links to ransomware deployment, including operations that have used the BlackCat, Embargo and Hunters International families against victim networks. The group operates as an affiliate-style actor: it gains entry, escalates, moves laterally into identity and backup infrastructure, and then hands the environment over to encryption or extortion tooling. Reported entry vectors include exploitation of unpatched internet-facing services and the abuse of legitimate remote access, followed by credential theft, creation of new privileged accounts and tampering with backup or recovery systems so that restoration is harder. Activity has been described in hybrid environments where on-premises identity and cloud tenant resources are joined, allowing the actor to move between the two. Evidence of this behaviour appears in identity provider sign-in and audit logs, endpoint process creation records, backup service configuration changes, and network traffic to command and control infrastructure.

beginner.definition: Storm-0501 is the name Microsoft gave to a criminal group that breaks into company networks and then locks the files for money. The group usually does not write its own ransomware. It prepares the way, and then other criminals run the attack. Security companies say it has worked with several well known ransomware families.
beginner.whyItMatters: Ransomware stops a business from working. If patient records, invoices or deliveries depend on those files, people are affected straight away. Storm-0501 also attacks backups, so a company may find that its safety copy is gone. Paying does not always bring the data back, and it funds more crime.
howItWorks: The group finds a way in, often through a service that was never patched.
It steals usernames and passwords, then makes its own hidden admin account.
The attackers move from one computer to another until they reach important systems.
They look for backups and try to damage or delete the copies.
They steal files first, so they can threaten to publish them later.
Finally they run ransomware to lock everything and demand payment.
beginner.example: Think of an office building at night. A thief finds a back window that the staff forgot to fix. Inside, they do not grab the safe straight away. First they copy every key, make their own spare key, and quietly take the backup tapes out of the storage room. Only then do they chain the doors and leave a note asking for money. That patient way of working is how Storm-0501 behaves.
takeaways: Patching internet-facing services quickly removes the easiest way in for groups like this.
Backups must be offline or immutable, because attackers go after them on purpose.
Watch for new admin accounts and unusual sign-ins, not just for encrypted files.

objectives: Explain how a ransomware affiliate prepares a network before encryption begins.
Describe why identity systems and backups are primary targets for Storm-0501.
Identify the log sources that reveal this group's activity early.
Summarise the risks of a hybrid environment where on-premises and cloud identity are joined.
Propose controls that limit lateral movement after an initial compromise.
Describe the extortion model that combines stolen data with encryption.
